name: Tandy 1000
credits: Layout after the original Tandy 1000 (1984) 90-key keyboard, as on the 1000, 1000A and 1000SX, checked against the deskthority wiki photograph (deskthority.net/wiki/Tandy_1000); colours after its light beige case, cream letter and keypad caps, darker beige function and modifier caps and dark grey legends.
notes: Faithful: the 90 keys in the photographed arrangement, which differs from the commonly remembered one: F1 to F12 in one row across the top with INSERT, DELETE and BREAK at its right; ALT and PRINT at the top right of the main block beside BACK SPACE; HOLD and NUM LOCK beside the tall ENTER; CAPS at the bottom left before SHIFT; the four arrows in the bottom row and the column above (↑ over ↓, between ENTER and the keypad); HOME beside ↑; the numeric keypad with PG UP, END and PG DN over 9, 1 and 3 and its own ENTER. There is no backslash, bar, tilde or backquote key in the main block: as on the machine they are the shifted legends of keypad 7, 4, 8 and 2, and shift on those keys types them. Zeros are the slashed Ø legend and type 0. Cream letter and keypad caps, darker beige modifiers, upper-case legends that type lower case (SHIFT and CAPS give capitals) and a blank space bar. Approximated: widths are compressed to fit a phone; the gaps between the F1-F4, F5-F8 and F9-F12 groups and before INSERT are closed up, since a row cannot hold a gap, so the F keys are a little wider than the letters; the big ENTER is two keys joined into one tall key, straight-sided rather than the machine's L; colours are by eye from one photograph. ↑ and ↓ step through the command history, ← and → move along the line, ENTER is return, ESC is escape and DELETE erases the last character (there is no forward delete). Mapped to none: F1 to F12 (decorative keys that can be pressed but type nothing), INSERT, BREAK, HOLD, PRINT (shifted too), ALT, CTRL, TAB, NUM LOCK and HOME; keypad keys type their digits whatever the NUM LOCK state. The badge strip is not drawn and no Tandy word mark appears.
